reading: Every object shifts one column to the left (cells pushed past the left edge are lost), then all background 0 cells become 5.
why: output = input translated by (0,-1) with clipping, every remaining 0 becomes 5

reading: Each row takes the colour of its nearest full-width stripe row; rows equidistant from two differently coloured stripes become all 1; in the vertical line column 8 and 1 swap (stripe rows become 1 with 8 at the crossing, other rows get 1 there).

slots.stripes: full rows of a non-background colour crossing the vertical 8 line
slots.fill: each background row gets the colour of the nearest stripe (ties of different colours -> whole row 1)
slots.line: vertical line column: 8->1 on non-stripe rows, stripe rows become all 1 except 8 at the crossing

why: on every pair each row's colour equals the nearest stripe colour, with stripes and the line swapped to 1/8
invariants: position of the vertical line and stripe rows

reading: There are two shape types in two colours; every copy of shape A is replaced by shape B (in B's colour) in the same bounding box, and vice versa.

slots.shape_a: the object shape of the first colour
slots.shape_b: the object shape of the second colour
slots.placement: each object is replaced, at its own bounding-box top-left, by the other colour's shape and colour

why: each object's box holds the other colour's shape in the output; nothing else changes

reading: Each isolated cell moves by a fixed offset that depends on its colour: 7 up 2, 9 down 2, 2 left 2, 1 right 1.
why: every marker reappears at its colour's offset and its old cell becomes background

reading: Each 1 sitting on top of a 5 stem drops to the bottom row, replacing the 5 there; its old cell becomes 0.
why: each colour-1 cell ends in the bottom row of its column; the cell it left is background
invariants: the 5 stems above the bottom row

reading: Colour-2 cells form loose clusters (2s within 2 cells of each other); inside each cluster's bounding box every non-2 cell becomes 4.

new_rows.name: box2
new_rows.datalog:
two(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, 2).
near(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- two(Y, X), two(Y2, X2), DY = Y2 - Y, DX = X2 - X, DY >= -2, DY <= 2, DX >= -2, DX <= 2.
reach(Y, X, Y2, X2) :- near(Y, X, Y2, X2).
reach(Y, X, Y3, X3) :- reach(Y, X, Y2, X2), near(Y2, X2, Y3, X3).
gid(Y, X, min(K)) :- reach(Y, X, Y2, X2), K = Y2 * 100 + X2.
gy0(G, min(Y)) :- gid(Y, X, G).
gy1(G, max(Y)) :- gid(Y, X, G).
gx0(G, min(X)) :- gid(Y, X, G).
gx1(G, max(X)) :- gid(Y, X, G).
box2(Y, X) :- gy0(G, A), gy1(G, B), gx0(G, L), gx1(G, R), px(Y, X, C), Y >= A, Y <= B, X >= L, X <= R, !two(Y, X).

why: exactly the non-2 cells inside each 2-cluster box change, all to 4

reading: A new 5 bar rising from the bottom row is drawn two columns right of the rightmost bar; its height is (number of 8 cells) minus (number of 2 cells).

slots.height: count of 8 cells - count of 2 cells

why: on every pair the only change is that 5 bar

reading: Every background cell that touches the shape only diagonally (no orthogonal fg neighbour) is painted with the shape's inner (minority) colour.

new_rows.name: halo
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
anyn(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, P), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, fgc(Y2, X2).
orthn(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, P), off(DY, DX), DY = 0, Y2 = Y, X2 = X + DX, fgc(Y2, X2).
orthn(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, P), off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X, fgc(Y2, X2).
halo(Y, X) :- anyn(Y, X), !orthn(Y, X), !fgc(Y, X).

slots.colour: the inner colour of the shape (2 in pair 0, 1 in pair 1)

why: exactly the diagonal-only background neighbours change, all to the inner colour

reading: The two-colour square object gets a surrounding band in its inner colour; the band thickness equals the inner core's smaller side, capped by the room to the nearest grid edge.

new_rows.name: ring
new_rows.datalog:
fgc(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
touchbg(C) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, px(Y2, X2, B), !fgc(Y2, X2).
innerc(C) :- cell(Y, X, C), !touchbg(C).
iy0(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C), innerc(C).
iy1(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C), innerc(C).
ix0(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C), innerc(C).
ix1(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C), innerc(C).
oy0(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
oy1(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
ox0(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
ox1(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
gy(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
gx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
cand(V) :- iy0(A), iy1(B), V = B - A + 1.
cand(V) :- ix0(A), ix1(B), V = B - A + 1.
cand(V) :- oy0(V).
cand(V) :- ox0(V).
cand(V) :- gy(G), oy1(B), V = G - B.
cand(V) :- gx(G), ox1(B), V = G - B.
th(min(V)) :- cand(V).
ring(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, P), !fgc(Y, X), th(T), oy0(A), oy1(B), ox0(L), ox1(R), Y0 = A - T, Y1 = B + T, X0 = L - T, X1 = R + T, Y >= Y0, Y <= Y1, X >= X0, X <= X1.

slots.colour: the inner colour (the object colour that never touches background)

why: exactly the background cells within T of the object's box change, all to the inner colour
invariants: cells farther than T from the object

reading: Each 8 L-tromino is completed to a 2x2 square by colouring its missing corner 1.

new_rows.name: hole
new_rows.datalog: hole(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0), off(DY, DX), Y1 = Y + DY, X1 = X + DX, cell(Y1, X, C), cell(Y, X1, C), cell(Y1, X1, C).

why: exactly the empty cell of each 2x2 window with three 8s becomes 1
